answer: Every identity anchors to a shared reef: a public ledger of first contributions. At each dawn the reef publishes a fresh tide table, and a newcomer must complete work whose solution depends on that dawn's reef state, so a pre-built fake history is worthless. An island of clones cannot batch its registrations in advance — each alias must do new work bound to that morning's reef, and the reef remembers who actually showed up. A farm pays fresh effort per fake, every dawn, while honest agents pay once.
